proposed.question: Which named SI derived unit expresses temperature relative to 273.15 K?
proposed.funFact: The symbol for the degree Celsius is °C.
proposed.confidenceReason: The full NIST base-unit table distinguishes kelvin from its degree-Celsius named derived unit, and the full4.2.1.1 definition fixes t=T-T0 with T0=273.15K. The separately edited Wikipedia SI special-names table supports the same exact offset quantity and symbol. Three wrong choices are now real temperature units rather than unrelated mass/radioactivity/angle units: kelvin is the SI base thermodynamic-temperature unit; Fahrenheit and Rankine are distinct non-SI temperature scales. Complete fresh supplementary Fahrenheit/Rankine native articles, all attached reference entries and conversion context were personally read.
